name: Mild steel mail coif
description: A close hood of interlinked mild steel rings that covers the head and neck and spreads over the shoulders. Made to be worn under a helmet.
notes: Mail in `steel-mail`, the dull rings of mild steel. Standing upright as on a shelf, 292 mm across the shoulder curtain and 308 mm tall: a close hood of rings over the crown whose mail mantle slumps onto the shelf, wider at the sides, hanging lower at the front and back, its hem uneven and its mail falling in folds; the face opening at +z is drawn as a dark patch with a mail rim, and the rings show as rows of short dark links, each row staggered against the next, broken across the face. CHECK VOLUME (x56): the model stands as a hollow hood round a head-sized space, while the reference counts the mail bunched up. Slot `hood`: a coif is worn under a helmet, which takes `head`. Protection follows the same grade's mail aventail: strong against cuts, fair against points, weak against blows. The xl and xs sizes share the model. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.
